summary: Persist Core witness registration and report qdevice status without enabling two-host fencing proof

guide.reason: The guide describes Core-owned witness registration, current status, runtime CA rotation and the unavailable automatic witness fence path.

api.reason: PoolMembership.Witness, the member-addressed sealed qdevice credential in authority replicas, and Core's reported cluster status extend existing report and peer contracts. Controller's new candidate/register routes have their own assessment. Older Core omits these fields; no witness readiness is inferred from omission.

roadmap.reason: The two-host plan remains partial; neither witness proof nor automatic takeover is accepted.

state.reason: The pool master owns selected witness kind, address, native CA pin, generation and credential readiness; member-specific PKCS#12 bundles are sealed in Core authority replicas. The Controller keeps only runtime qnetd CA material.
state.record: Core pool-peer.json PoolMembership.Witness on the master and signed per-member pool authority replicas; a fresh Controller reconstructs the pool witness record from the master's authenticated managed membership report and Core re-registers after Controller CA rotation.

verification.method: Focused protocol and agent witness tests passed before the workstation test escape; subsequent work used static review, the 74-case API contract suite, generated-reference check, privacy check and compile-only Go checks. An independent reviewer checked two-host freeze topology and withheld SBD/proof. No Core-to-Controller deployment, one-host-down qnetd outage, hardware reset or browser acceptance is claimed; host-affecting tests are suspended.
